items.title: George "Kid Sheik" Colar Interview, 1958-07-20
items.q: Sometimes Sam Morgan, Chris Kelly, Kid Rene, all of them meet up on the corner together, advertising for three different dances

ctx.x: Yeah, he played it as an inch. Talking about Kid Renné, what was in, in those days when his lip was real hard and all that, when he was really in his heyday, what was his strongest point, what was his specialty? Was it out in the streets, or was it playing the blues, or was it playing jitney dance as fast as...

Oh no, see, Renné never did work with no jitney dancer. No, he never did work with that. All of his work was economy hall, copper, and his dance meetings. He never did work with them jitney, he never did work with that. He was a dance hall, advertising, Perez, and all. He never worked at that. And he was a standout man in all his execution. Any number, he was a standout man. He had to like to hear him play . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . clean trumpet players out on them fellas. I wouldn't say he was the best…
Was Buddy Petit still very active in those things?
